key_insight: A conformal prediction–enabled random forest prospectively classified multiple sclerosis disease course with calibrated uncertainty, closely matching clinician-recorded labels.
clinical_relevance: This could help standardize secondary progressive MS identification and support earlier, more consistent decision-making in registry and clinical workflows.
method: Trained and calibrated on Swedish MS Registry 2022 data.
Prospectively validated on an independent 2025 registry cohort not used in training.
Compared performance against clinician labels and Lorscheider criteria.
evidence_signal: Using 10,787 people for training/calibration and 15,719 for prospective validation, the model achieved 92% RRMS and 95% SPMS visit-level accuracy, with 98% sensitivity and 89% specificity at the individual level.
watch_item: Although promising, performance was evaluated against registry clinician-recorded labels and may require further external validation before broader clinical implementation.
paper_title: Prospective validation of an uncertainty-aware machine learning model for secondary progressive multiple sclerosis classification
